memory_update.text: For vertical AI automation software, keep PLTR as the reference benchmark but avoid allowing it to crowd out smaller deployment-layer names.
PATH belongs in the underfollowed lane as a possible agentic workflow automation deployment layer; survival depends on ARR growth and net retention improving beyond 107%.
SOUN is a speculative-shadow candidate in conversational and voice AI workflow automation; key proof points are LivePerson integration, recurring revenue quality, and enterprise retention.
C3.ai is a small-cap enterprise AI applications candidate with vertical/federal exposure, but requires stronger evidence of durable subscription growth and operating leverage.
Next pass should search for lower-attention data governance, model observability, AI security, document/workflow automation, and industrial software names where AI revenue attach rates are disclosed.

node: Vertical AI automation software, data governance, industrial workflow, and model deployment tools
summary: Layer 1B expands the software-side stock universe for AI workflow deployment beyond hyperscalers and semiconductor leaders. The reference anchor is Palantir, because its AIP adoption provides the clearest public-market proof that enterprises are paying for operational AI, not just model access. The underfollowed lane focuses on smaller US-listed companies where the chokepoint is not compute supply, but deployment into regulated workflows, automation systems, customer-service operations, industrial/federal processes, and governed enterprise data. These are research candidates only, not trading recommendations.
